q-135478.worked_solution:
We need to isolate the variable $u.$ To do this, we treat $v$ as though it were a constant and apply the addition and multiplication principles as usual.

In this case, we simply subtract $\frac{v}{2}$ from both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u+\frac{v}{2} & =1 \\ u+\frac{v}{2}-\frac{v}{2} & =1-\frac{v}{2} \\ u+0 & =1-\frac{v}{2} \\ u & =1-\frac{v}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

q-135010.name: Question 3
q-135010.worked_solution:
We need to isolate the variable $x.$ To do this, we treat $y$ as though it were a constant and apply the addition and multiplication principles as usual.

First, we add $5y$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}-5y & =2y \\ \frac{x}{2}-5y+5y & =2y+5y \\ \frac{x}{2} & =2y+5y \\ \frac{x}{2} & =7y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we multiply both sides of the equation by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & =7y \\ 2\cdot \frac{x}{2} & =2\cdot 7y \\ \cancel{2}\cdot \frac{x}{\cancel{2}} & =2\cdot 7y \\ x & =2\cdot 7y \\ x & =14y\end{aligned}
$$

q-2611.name: Question 4
q-2611.worked_solution:
We need to isolate the variable $y.$ To do this, we treat $x$ as though it were a constant and apply the addition and multiplication principles as usual.

First, we subtract $6x$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}6x+3y & =3 \\ 6x+3y-6x & =3-6x \\ 6x-6x+3y & =3-6x \\ 3y & =3-6x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by $3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3y & =3-6x \\ 3y & =3(1-2x) \\ \frac{3y}{3} & =\frac{3(1-2x)}{3} \\ \frac{\cancel{3}y}{\cancel{3}} & =\frac{\cancel{3}(1-2x)}{\cancel{3}} \\ y & =1-2x\end{aligned}
$$

q-176623.name: Question 5
q-176623.worked_solution:
We need to isolate the variable $x.$ First, we cross-multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+1}{3} & =\frac{y-x}{2} \\ 2\cdot (2x+1) & =3\cdot (y-x) \\ 4x+2 & =3y-3x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we subtract $2$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+2 & =3y-3x \\ 4x+2-2 & =3y-3x-2 \\ 4x & =3y-3x-2\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we add $3x$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & =3y-3x-2 \\ 4x+3x & =3y-3x-2+3x \\ 7x & =3y-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides of the equation by $7:$

$$
\begin{aligned}7x & =3y-2 \\ \frac{7x}{7} & =\frac{3y-2}{7} \\ \frac{\cancel{7}x}{\cancel{7}} & =\frac{3y-2}{7} \\ x & =\frac{3y-2}{7}\end{aligned}
$$
